facts.raw_span: a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
The specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm and had a 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Revealed a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Showed positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor
Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells
Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A

concepts.why: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, pedunculated mass with anaplastic cells and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers supports the diagnosis of malignant melanoma of the caruncle.
The absence of pigmentation and the presence of anaplastic cells with mitotic activity, along with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers, support the diagnosis of amelanotic melanoma.
Although there is no evidence of PAM, the presence of a melanocytic lesion with atypical features and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers warrants consideration of a PAM-like lesion.
The presence of a melanocytic lesion with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and the absence of tumor in conjunctival biopsies support the diagnosis of melanoma of the conjunctiva.
The presence of a solid tumor with anaplastic cells and mitotic activity supports the diagnosis of an anaplastic tumor of the caruncle.

The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, and necrotic tumor with a high proliferative index, as indicated by the Ki-67 proliferation marker, points towards an aggressive melanoma, specifically anaplastic melanoma.

rationales.F01: Rapid growth of the lesion suggests malignancy, but is not specific to any particular diagnosis.
rationales.F02: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface is highly suggestive of an amelanotic melanoma.
rationales.F05: The presence of a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity, is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F06: The positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A is highly suggestive of a melanoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of a mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F12: The presence of melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A is highly suggestive of a melanoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle, along with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers and a high proliferative index, strongly supports Malignant Melanoma of the Caruncle, with Anaplastic Melanoma as a close runner-up due to the anaplastic nature of the tumor cells.
